items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: Benny Morten and myself were working for Chick at the Roseland. So we made a trade.

ctx.x: Within a few blocks of each other. Everybody lived around the corner and down here and you'd bump into each other, you know, so I got to know all the musicians, not real well, some of them. It was -- and I remember that it was a real honor to me, to meet Donald Redman, even moreso than Fletcher Henderson, because he was such a great musician. Oh, he could play trumpet, piano, clarinet, saxophone, and one of the greatest arrangers, you know. That type of man is just a wonderful, talented person, and I thought a…

The way he hired me, he -- I don't remember exactly how -- I just don't remember the point when he -- when he offered me the job, but this was a period where I call it the Big Trade. The Big Trade was Benny Carter and Jimmy Harrison, Jimmy Harrison the trombone player, they were working for Fletcher at Connie's Inn, and Benny Morten and myself were
working for Chick at the Roseland. So we made a trade. Benny Carter and Jimmy Harrison for Russell Procope and Benny Martin. So we switched jobs. That's what we always called the Big Trade.
